name: Nathan
description: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy

points: Nathan told David to do all that was in his heart, for the Lord was with him. But that night the word of the Lord came to Nathan.

note.label: 2 Samuel 7: The Covenant With the House of David

points: Nathan came to David with a parable. When David judged that the man deserved to die for taking the poor man's one lamb, he was unknowingly pronouncing sentence on himself.

note.label: 2 Samuel 12: Nathan's Parable and the Judgment on David's House

points: The Lord sent Nathan unto David with the parable of the rich man who spared his own flock and took the poor man's one little ewe lamb. David's anger was greatly kindled: the man that hath done this thing shall surely die. And Nathan said, thou art the man. The rich man is you, David; the poor man was Uriah the Hittite, and the ewe lamb was his wife.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: Nathan said unto David, Thou art the man. Thus saith the Most High: I anointed thee king over Israel, delivered thee out of the hand of Saul, gave thee thy master's house and wives, and the house of Israel and of Judah, and would have given thee more. Wherefore hast thou despised the commandment to do evil, killing Uriah the Hittite with the sword and taking his wife, slaying him with the sword of the children of Ammon?

note.label: 2 Samuel 12: Nathan's Parable and the Judgment on David's House

points: Nathan had to approach David with a parable, because at this point David was out of his right mind; approach him the wrong way and he could have been killed too. Once the example gave David conviction, he came to his senses: I have sinned against the Lord.

The Lord said, what thou didst secretly, I will do this thing before all Israel: the sword shall never depart from thine house. And Nathan said, the Lord also hath put away thy sin; thou shalt not die. But evil stayed in David's house perpetually: the trouble among his sons, his own counsellor turning against him, being chased out of his kingdom. David was never the same after this.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: David commands that Solomon be set on the king's own mule and brought to Gihon, where Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him king over Israel. The people come up rejoicing so that the earth rings with the sound.

note.label: 1 Kings 1: A King Exalts Himself and a King Is Anointed

points: David told Nathan the prophet that he dwelt in a house of cedars while the ark remained under curtains.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 17: The Most High Will Build David a House

points: Nathan first answered that David should do all in his heart, for the Most High was with him.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 17: The Most High Will Build David a House

points: That same night the word of the Most High came to Nathan, saying David should not build him a house to dwell in.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 17: The Most High Will Build David a House

points: The rest of the acts of Solomon are written in the book of Nathan the prophet, the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and the visions of Iddo the seer against Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: Hezekiah sets the Levites in the house of the Lord with cymbals, psalteries, and harps according to the commandment of David, Gad the seer, and Nathan the prophet.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 29: Hezekiah Cleanses the House of the Lord

points: To the chief musician, a Psalm of David, written after Nathan the prophet came to him following his sin with Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah one of the soldiers in David's army.
Nathan got on David about it and corrected him. Now David sends up this prayer, asking the Most High for forgiveness.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed
